body: [{"streamId":"01a0c941-fb35-751b-8179-9227d2ef970d","eventTypeName":"Hall9k.Domain.Features.Decision.DecisionRecorded","eventDataJson":"{\u0022Id\u0022:\u002201a0c941-fb35-751b-8179-9227d2ef970d\u0022,\u0022Scope\u0022:\u0022Project\u0022,\u0022ScopeId\u0022:\u002201a00d41-5d9a-73cc-b648-af431f721a71\u0022,\u0022Statement\u0022:\u0022**A review-feedback follow-up never answers a human reviewer in the owner\\u0027s name on its own: a thread a person opened that asks nothing, beside a review of theirs that asks nothing, dispatches no lap at all; and a lap that declines or routes a person\\u0027s thread drafts the reply and parks it for the owner to send, edit, or drop.** (2026-09-15, task 7d8d1fec, walked by the hall9k project window the same day at Brian\\u0027s priority.) Why: two accurate replies that still had to be deleted. arx-platform PR #2021, 2026-09-09 \\u2014 John Mark approves at 10:11 and opens one thread saying his own pull request needs the same pattern; closeout reopens the task at 10:14 on one unresolved human thread; the follow-up disposes it decline (correct), pushes nothing (correct), and posts about 400 words under Brian\\u0027s login at 10:16, which he deletes at 10:21 and replaces with his own line. arx-platform PR #2042, 2026-09-15 \\u2014 jsmotherman approves at 11:29 and asks in a thread why a canary value rather than the sentinel; run 01a0a5ae posts a five-paragraph answer under Brian\\u0027s login at 11:31. Neither reply was wrong. The defect is that a person addressed Brian and something else answered as him, with no operator lever between the dispatch and the post. **The thread that buys no lap.** \\u0060AdvisoryReviewThreads.Advisory\\u0060 classifies an unresolved thread a person opened as advisory when the thread\\u0027s own OPENING comment asks nothing and that same person has no standing request for change on the pull request and asked for none in the words of their latest review; \\u0060CloseoutEngine.OutstandingReviewThreadIds\\u0060 then excludes it from the dispatch decision exactly as it already excludes a thread this run declined or routed (#159). The test errs toward dispatching at every step \\u2014 an unreadable thread, a reviewer the snapshot does not list, a body the provider never reported, a question mark anywhere, any of a short list of request phrasings, any of a second list of defect claims (\\u0022off by one\\u0022, \\u0022throws\\u0022, \\u0022swallows\\u0022, \\u0022stale\\u0022), or a bare imperative in the imperative position \\u2014 the start of the text, a fresh line, or a new sentence (\\u0022Rename this to \\u0060Canonical\\u0060.\\u0022, \\u0022Add a null check here.\\u0022, \\u0022Use the sentinel instead.\\u0022) \\u2014 all come back \\u0022asks something\\u0022, which is the behaviour that existed before \\u2014 because a false advisory costs a person an unanswered question while a false ask costs one lap that drafts and parks. Bare \\u0022needs\\u0022 is deliberately not a request phrase: \\u0022my own PR needs the same pattern\\u0022 is the first incident\\u0027s exact wording and is a remark about somebody else\\u0027s branch. **It shapes dispatch and nothing else.** The thread stays unresolved in \\u0060UnresolvedReviewThreadCount\\u0060, so the merge bar is untouched and a pre-approved merge still waits on it; the classification rides on \\u0060AdvisoryReviewThreadsObserved\\u0060 (appended only when the set changes, since the sweep re-reads every poll interval) so \\u0060h9k status\\u0060 and \\u0060h9k task show\\u0060 can say \\u00221 human thread asks nothing, not dispatched\\u0022 rather than showing an unanswered person beside no activity, which reads as the machinery having missed them. **The park.** A lap that disposes a person\\u0027s thread decline or route writes the same \\u0060DISAGREEMENT:\\u0060 block #152 already defined, now carrying \\u0060disposition=\\u0060, and closes \\u0060RESOLUTION: disputed\\u0060; \\u0060RunSupervisor.HumanThreadReplyDrafts\\u0060 keeps only the blocks whose \\u0060thread=\\u0060 names a thread CLOSEOUT itself observed a person opening (\\u0060TaskReopened.HumanReviewThreads\\u0060, the provider\\u0027s own actor type \\u2014 the session\\u0027s \\u0060kind=\\u0060 self-report gates nothing, per \\u0060ReviewThreadOutcome.IsHuman\\u0060\\u0027s own doc) and appends \\u0060HumanThreadReplyParked\\u0060 ahead of the \\u0060ReviewParked\\u0060 that moves the state. **The park does not depend on the session closing correctly.** The \\u0060DISAGREEMENT:\\u0060 block is the good path; a lap that wrote an honest \\u0060THREAD DISPOSITION: \\u2026 disposition=decline\\u0060 for a person\\u0027s thread and then closed \\u0060RESOLUTION: resolved\\u0060 used to park nothing, post nothing, and have the thread dropped from every later dispatch decision by the #159 already-answered exclusion \\u2014 the person answered by nobody, with nothing on the board saying a reply was owed. So \\u0060RunSupervisor\\u0060 reads the triage as a second source and parks on it too, with a draft carrying no proposed reply (the honest record: the lap composed none, and \\u0060h9k review resolve\\u0060 refuses \\u0060--post-reply-as-written\\u0060 on a blank draft so the operator writes the reply or drops it), and \\u0060CloseoutEngine.OutstandingReviewThreadIds\\u0060 now excludes a declined or routed human thread only when this run actually discharged it \\u2014 a reply recorded through \\u0060h9k pr reply\\u0060, or a drafted reply parked for the owner. With neither, the thread stays outstanding and keeps buying a lap, the same fallback a bot thread whose resolve mutation never landed already takes. Its own event rather than \\u0060ReviewDisagreementParked\\u0060, because these drafts answer no changes-requested review and rendering them under one would say a review existed; everything downstream is shared on purpose \\u2014 both land in \\u0060RunAggregate.ParkedDisagreements\\u0060, both set \\u0060ParkedOnReviewDisagreement\\u0060, and both take the same three \\u0060h9k review resolve\\u0060 choices, so the operator learns one lever. A block naming no disposition is still the older undecidable-design-call dispute (#62) and still takes the plain park, which asks for a verdict rather than for words. **The enforcement.** The prompt is not the only thing holding this. Every in-thread reply a follow-up makes goes through \\u0060h9k pr reply \\u003Ctask\\u003E --thread \\u003Cid\\u003E --disposition fix|decline|route --body \\u0022\\u003Ctext\\u003E\\u0022\\u0060, which refuses a decline or a route into a thread the platform observed a person opening, records the refusal with the thread id (\\u0060ReviewThreadReplyRefused\\u0060, rendered by \\u0060h9k task show\\u0060), and posts nothing; the shell\\u0027s own routes to a thread \\u2014 the REST replies endpoint, the REST inline-comment and review endpoints when they carry a write parameter (\\u0060in_reply_to\\u0060, \\u0060commit_id\\u0060, \\u0060event=\\u0060, \\u0060body=\\u0060, each matched only where a value is actually assigned to it, so filtering a read on \\u0060.in_reply_to_id\\u0060 is not a write), every \\u0060addPullRequestReview\\u2026\\u0060 mutation matched on the shared prefix, \\u0060gh pr review\\u0060 \\u2014 are refused by a \\u0060PreToolUse\\u0060 hook (\\u0060ClaudeSettingsFile.ReviewThreadReplyGuardHook\\u0060, \\u0060h9k pr reply-guard\\u0060) written into every follow-up\\u0027s settings file. A hook and not a \\u0060permissions.deny\\u0060 entry for two reasons, both fatal to the deny: the reply route is routinely spelled with the path in quotes, which no prefix rule matches, and \\u0060--dangerously-skip-permissions\\u0060 voids the permission engine outright while leaving hooks running. The matcher names both shell tools, \\u0060Bash|PowerShell\\u0060, and \\u0060PullRequestReplyGuardCommand\\u0060 answers for both: on this platform\\u0027s own primary host a dispatched session is handed a PowerShell tool beside its Bash one and the same \\u0060gh api \\u2026/replies\\u0060 line runs in either, so a Bash-only matcher was a guard with the ordinary Windows shell left open beside it. The hook fails OPEN everywhere \\u2014 missing binary, unparseable payload, a tool that is neither shell \\u2014 because blocking every command in every follow-up on a mis-parse is a worse failure than the one it prevents. A refusal takes both halves \\u2014 a route AND something that can actually reach GitHub\\u0027s API (\\u0060gh api\\u0060, \\u0060curl\\u0060, \\u0060wget\\u0060, a spelled \\u0060api.github.com\\u0060) \\u2014 because every identifier the guard matches is also source text in this repository, and matching the route alone refused \\u0060git grep addPullRequestReviewThreadReply\\u0060 for what it never sent. Two holes are named rather than papered over: \\u0060gh pr comment\\u0060 is left alone because a review BODY is unthreadable and answering one is an instruction older than this entry (#62), and the disposition is the session\\u0027s own word \\u2014 so every accepted reply records the claim (\\u0060ReviewThreadReplyPosted\\u0060) and \\u0060RunSupervisor\\u0060 compares it against the same thread\\u0027s own \\u0060THREAD DISPOSITION:\\u0060 block at completion, putting a reply that claimed fix and was really a decline in the run log rather than nowhere. **What is untouched.** Bot-authored threads keep #159 whole: evidence in, thread resolved, nobody waiting. A fix\\u0027s reply posts in anyone\\u0027s thread, because \\u0022I changed it, here is what changed\\u0022 invites no argument and the commit is the evidence. The merge bar is unchanged, and a human thread beside \\u0060CHANGES_REQUESTED\\u0060, or any human thread that asks a question or a change, still dispatches exactly as it did. **Does this block the later vision?** No \\u2014 additive throughout: one optional field on \\u0060TaskReopened\\u0060, one on the snapshot, four new run events, two new CLI commands, and a pull request whose human threads all ask something behaves as it did before. ruled 2026-09-13 (\\u0060a2-team-half-walk-2026-09-13.md\\u0060) as the team half of A2a\\u0027s identity work, split from T2\\u0027s invite flow (stacked on this one, not yet built). **The trust files.** \\u0060owners/\\u003Croot\\u003E/nodes/\\u003Cnode-id\\u003E.yaml\\u0060 (node id, node public key, issued at) vouches a node into an owner\\u0027s own fleet, and \\u0060owners/\\u003Croot\\u003E/revoked/\\u003Cnode-id\\u003E.yaml\\u0060 revokes one, both on the existing \\u0060refs/hall9k/ledger/owners/\\u003Croot\\u003E\\u0060 ref (A2a); the latest of the two, in that ref\\u0027s own commit order, wins, so a surviving node undoes a bad revocation by vouching again. Project membership is a new ref, \\u0060refs/hall9k/ledger/members\\u0060 (registered in \\u0060LedgerRefRegistry\\u0060, A1\\u0027s one place), holding one \\u0060members/\\u003Croot-fingerprint\\u003E.yaml\\u0060 per member (root fingerprint, role owner or member, issued at); a member removal deletes that file outright rather than writing a tombstone, which is why \\u0060ILedger\\u0060 gains \\u0060DeleteAsync\\u0060/\\u0060LedgerDeleteRequest\\u0060 alongside the existing \\u0060WriteAsync\\u0060 (\\u0060GitLedger.BuildDeleteTreeAsync\\u0060 rebuilds the tree from the parent\\u0027s own \\u0060ls-tree\\u0060 listing through \\u0060update-index --index-info\\u0060, never \\u0060read-tree\\u0060 plus \\u0060update-index --force-remove\\u0060, which git refuses outright in a bare repository even though nothing about it touches a working tree). **The chain reader.** \\u0060Hall9k.Connectors.Trust.GitLedgerChainReader\\u0060 discovers every owner root a project\\u0027s ledger has ever seen (one \\u0060ls-remote\\u0060 against \\u0060refs/hall9k/ledger/owners/*\\u0060), computes each root\\u0027s own chain independent of project membership (self-certification: the ref name, the declared key\\u0027s own fingerprint, and the commit introducing \\u0060root.yaml\\u0060 all have to agree, then every vouch or revocation in that ref\\u0027s own history, oldest first, accepted only when its signer already belongs to the chain being built), then replays \\u0060refs/hall9k/ledger/members\\u0060 against those chains: the ref\\u0027s own literal first commit touching a members file is genesis, self-written, unconditional either way, spent whether it succeeds or not; every later write needs a signer that is, as of this read, an Owner-role member\\u0027s own root key or a node currently in that root\\u0027s own chain \\u2014 the chain\\u0027s live state at read time, never a snapshot pinned to that write\\u0027s own claimed committer date (a field its writer freely chooses) \\u2014 so a later self-claimed owner with no vouch is ignored. \\u0060TrustChain.IsAllowedSigner\\u0060 restricts an owner\\u0027s own chain to project members, which is what makes a stranger\\u0027s internally self-consistent root and node file count for nothing anywhere in this project. **The write-side refusal.** \\u0060h9k node vouch \\u003Cnode-id\\u003E\\u0060 and \\u0060h9k node revoke \\u003Cnode-id\\u003E\\u0060 (a new \\u0060node\\u0060 command group) write into every non-archived project this owner is registered to, the same shape \\u0060h9k project join\\u0060\\u0027s own root retirement already uses, and refuse before any push, naming the rule, when this node\\u0027s own key is not itself enrolled in that owner\\u0027s own chain. \\u0060h9k project members\\u0060 (root, login when known from a local \\u0060OwnerDetails\\u0060 match, role, nodes, verified state) and \\u0060h9k project member remove \\u003Cfingerprint\\u003E\\u0060 (owner role only, deleting the file) round out the group; \\u0060h9k project join\\u0060 now also writes the genesis members file itself when it establishes a brand-new root. **The upgrade.** \\u0060GitLedgerMessageTransport.ReadSinceAsync\\u0060 still reads a sender\\u0027s candidate key from its own self-announced node file, but now also asks a \\u0060GitLedgerChainReader\\u0060 whether that key is \\u0060IsAllowedSigner\\u0060 before ever checking the commit\\u0027s own signature against it, replacing M1a\\u0027s node-level \\u0022does a node file exist\\u0022 with a genuine chain walk; \\u0060InMemoryMessageTransport\\u0060 gained the identical, optional check behind a nullable \\u0060ILedgerChainReader\\u0060 so every M1a/M1b seam test keeps its original node-file-only shape unless a test asks for more. **Events.** \\u0060NodeVouched\\u0060/\\u0060NodeRevoked\\u0060 on the Owner stream (owner-scoped, this node\\u0027s own audit trail; other nodes learn a vouch from the file, never from this event) and \\u0060MemberVouched\\u0060/\\u0060MemberRemoved\\u0060 on the Project stream (project-scoped, team-facing), all four classified in \\u0060EventScopeRegistry\\u0060. **Tests.** \\u0060GitLedgerChainReaderTests\\u0060 is the second place, besides \\u0060GitLedgerTests\\u0060, a throwaway bare repository is used at all (Brian\\u0027s 2026-09-13 testing rule), reusing \\u0060LedgerTestRepo\\u0060 directly rather than a second copy of the same helper, against three simulated nodes: a vouched second node verifies on a third node\\u0027s own independent read; a stranger\\u0027s root and node file are ignored everywhere; a member-role node cannot write a membership; revocation then re-vouch restores; genesis picks the first file by ref order. Everything above it (the CLI commands, the deciders, the message-transport upgrade) is tested through \\u0060FakeLedger\\u0060/\\u0060FakeLedgerChainReader\\u0060, never a real repository. \\u0060dotnet build\\u0060 and \\u0060dotnet test\\u0060 pass; the CLI reference and this entry are the one apiece this task owes. **Does this block the later vision?** No, with two known, accepted limits.
